newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU no word on Coke buy of CCSB, Virgin move.
newsitem.headline: EU no word on Coke buy of CCSB, Virgin move.

text.p: The European Commission declined to comment on Friday on Virgin Cola allegations that a British bottler of soft drinks which is to be controlled by Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc is abusing its dominant position.

The Commission also refused to unveil details about objections that it is expected to file shortly against Coca-Cola's proposed takeover of the company, Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages Ltd (CCSB), sticking to its policy of discretion in cases which are the subject of an in-depth probe.
Coca-Cola itself said in a quarterly filing to the Securities and Exchange Commission that it expected the EU statement before the end of November.

The Commission said on September 13 it was starting the so-called second stage of proceedings to assess the impact of the proposed acquisition on the conditions of competition for soft drinks in Britain.
Lawyers well versed in EU competition law stressed that it is normal procedure to follow that with a statement of objections detailing its grievances.

The opening of a detailed inquiry, which lasts up to four months, usually means that the deal is unlikely to get EU clearance without being changed. This often means selling off some businesses to avoid creation or strengthening of dominant positions.

However, in July the Commission cleared the mega merger between Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz requesting only that the companies undertake to grant licences for key animal drugs ingredients where they would have held a strong position.
Virgin said on Thursday it would complain to the Commission about what it sees as CCSB's abuse of its dominant position in Britain's cola market.
Virgin Cola, part of the Virgin Group run by millionaire entrepreneur Richard Branson, wants an investigation into CCSB's "anti-competitive practices," said a spokeswoman at Virgin Cola.
